Apple Intelligence engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Apple Intelligence rollout covers storefront language. Developer portal, Xcode, and Connect actually separate on-device AI behavior from product-page copy:

  • Foundation Models framework — on-device model APIs and inference hooks in the binary. Controls whether the app can call Apple Intelligence features. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • App Intents for Apple Intelligence — action surfaces that expose your app to system AI workflows. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains on-device intelligence to buyers.
  • Private Cloud Compute — server-side processing for certain Apple Intelligence tasks when on-device capacity is insufficient. Your listing may mention privacy-forward AI; configuring PCC is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, Visual Intelligence — system-level Apple Intelligence features your app may integrate with or complement. Listing copy may reference them as buyer benefits; building those integrations is platform and app engineering, not Connect metadata.
  • App Review AI disclosures — Connect questionnaires when your app uses generative AI. Filing accurate answers is compliance work — AppLocale does not complete disclosures for you.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Apple Intelligence capability flags.

A working Apple Intelligence integration and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
